title: Training Small Language Models for Transferable Tool Selection
title_zh: 训练小型语言模型实现可迁移的工具选择

paragraphs.en: As LLM agents operate over corpora of more than ten thousand tools, selecting the right tool for a complex multi-step user instruction becomes a central bottleneck. Tool descriptions cannot all fit in context, and relevance-based retrievers only rank tools without knowing which are actually needed. Recent work instead leverages proprietary commercial LLMs like Claude or ChatGPT to drive a retriever, decomposing the instruction and selecting over retrieved candidates. We show that a small, open model can be trained via reinforcement learning to perform the same functionality. On ToolBench, a Qwen3-8B model post-trained with our recipe outperforms Llama-4-Maverick (402B). In addition, the trained model transfers directly to different retrievers and generalizes to new tool corpora in different domains.
paragraphs.zh: 当大语言模型智能体在包含上万工具的语料库上运行时，如何为复杂的多步骤用户指令选择正确的工具成为一个核心瓶颈。 工具描述无法全部放入上下文中，而基于相关性的检索器只能对工具进行排序，并不知道哪些工具是实际需要的。 近期的工作转而利用 Claude 或 ChatGPT 等专有商业大语言模型来驱动检索器，对指令进行分解，并在检索到的候选项中进行选择。 我们证明，可以通过强化学习训练一个小型开源模型来执行相同的功能。 在 ToolBench 上，按照我们的方法训练后的 Qwen3-8B 模型优于 Llama-4-Maverick（402B）。 此外，训练后的模型可以直接迁移到不同的检索器，并能泛化到不同领域的新工具语料库。

paragraphs.en: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly solve user tasks by invoking external tools (or APIs) 1 1 1 ToolBench ( Qin et al., 2024 ) uses “tool” for a RapidAPI service that groups several APIs. In this paper the unit being selected is always an individual API, which we call a tool. e.g., sending an email, booking a flight, or fetching data from the web, rather than producing an answer from the model’s learned knowledge alone. As agents are applied to real software ecosystems, the number of callable tools has grown to well over ten thousand in some public tool corpora ( Qin et al., 2024 ; Shi et al., 2025 ) , and enterprises add proprietary tools for internal use. At this scale, the model’s context overflows if every tool description is placed in it, so selecting the right tool becomes a bottleneck that precedes the actual execution.
paragraphs.zh: 大语言模型（LLM）智能体越来越多地通过调用外部工具（或 API）来解决用户任务 1 1 1 ToolBench（Qin et al., 2024）将分组了多个 API 的 RapidAPI 服务称为“工具”。 在本文中，被选择的单元始终是单个 API，我们将其称为工具，例如发送电子邮件、预订航班或从网络获取数据，而不是仅依靠模型学到的知识来产生答案。 随着智能体被应用于真实的软件生态系统中，在一些公开工具语料库中可调用的工具数量已增长到远超一万个（Qin et al., 2024；Shi et al., 2025），并且企业还会添加供内部使用的专有工具。 在这种规模下，如果把每个工具的描述都放入模型的上下文中，上下文就会溢出，因此选择合适的工具成为先于实际执行的一个瓶颈。

paragraphs.en: The classical solution is a retriever , which scores each tool by its similarity to the user instruction and returns a small set of high-scoring candidates for the agent to choose from. Retrievers come in two broad families. Lexical retrievers such as BM25 (Best Matching 25) ( Robertson and Zaragoza, 2009 ) score a tool by how many query terms appear in its documentation, weighting rarer terms more heavily, and apply to any corpus without training. Dense retrievers such as COLT ( Qu et al., 2024 ) instead embed the instruction and each tool description into a shared vector space with an encoder trained on the target corpus, and rank tools by embedding similarity. LLMs have also been introduced to assist a fixed retriever by rewriting queries ( Chen et al., 2024 ; Kachuee et al., 2025 ) , expanding documents ( Lu et al., 2026 ; Senthil et al., 2026 ; Wu et al., 2025 ) , or re-ranking candidates ( Zheng et al., 2024b ) . However, a retriever can only assign a relevance-based ranking over tools; it does not know which of them the task actually requires. This is especially problematic when the user instruction contains multiple substeps and requires multiple tools.
paragraphs.zh: 经典的解决方案是检索器，它根据每个工具与用户指令的相似度进行打分，并返回少量高分候选工具供智能体选择。 检索器大致分为两大类。 诸如 BM25（Best Matching 25）（Robertson and Zaragoza, 2009）之类的词汇检索器根据查询词在工具文档中出现的数量为工具打分，对较罕见的词给予更高的权重，并且无需训练即可应用于任何语料库。 诸如 COLT（Qu et al., 2024）之类的稠密检索器则将在目标语料库上训练得到的编码器用于把指令和每个工具描述嵌入到一个共享向量空间中，并根据嵌入相似度对工具进行排序。 研究者还引入了大语言模型来辅助固定的检索器，方式包括重写查询（Chen et al., 2024；Kachuee et al., 2025）、扩展文档（Lu et al., 2026；Senthil et al., 2026；Wu et al., 2025）或对候选工具进行重排序（Zheng et al., 2024b）。 然而，检索器只能给出基于相关性的工具排序，它并不知道任务实际需要其中哪些工具。 当用户指令包含多个子步骤且需要多个工具时，这一问题尤为突出。

paragraphs.en: To address this, recent work places the LLM at the center of the selection workflow and uses the retriever as a meta-tool invoked on demand. Instead of consuming a single ranked list produced in one pass, the LLM drives retrieval across turns in a ReAct-style loop ( Braunschweiler et al., 2025 ; Lumer et al., 2025a ; Lumer et al., 2026 ) : a Plan stage decomposes the user instruction into substeps, a Retrieve stage fetches a set of relevant candidates, and a Select stage chooses the tools it judges necessary, repeating until the instruction is covered. Because the model, not the ranking function, decides which retrieved tools are required, this design directly handles the multi-substep, multi-tool instructions that a relevance ranking alone cannot address. Existing work performs tool selection with proprietary commercial models such as Claude or ChatGPT under careful prompt tuning. Since tool selection is a recurring sub-routine of the agentic tool-calling pipeline, we ask whether a small model can perform the task.
paragraphs.zh: 为解决这一问题，近期的工作将大语言模型置于选择工作流的中心，并把检索器作为一种按需调用的元工具。 大语言模型不再一次性消费单轮生成的排序列表，而是以 ReAct 风格的循环在多轮中驱动检索（Braunschweiler et al., 2025 ; Lumer et al., 2025a ; Lumer et al., 2026）：规划阶段将用户指令分解为若干子步骤，检索阶段获取一组相关候选，选择阶段挑选它认为必要的工具，如此重复直到指令被覆盖。 由于是由模型而非排序函数来决定需要哪些检索到的工具，这一设计能够直接处理仅靠相关性排序无法应对的多子步骤、多工具指令。 现有工作在细致的提示词调优下，使用 Claude 或 ChatGPT 等专有商业模型来执行工具选择。 由于工具选择是智能体工具调用流程中反复出现的子程序，我们想探究一个小模型能否完成这一任务。

paragraphs.en: Transferability across tool domains. A tool-selection model trained on one domain of tools should be usable directly on another, so that a separate model need not be trained for every tool corpus.
paragraphs.zh: 跨工具领域的可迁移性。 在某一工具领域上训练的工具选择模型应当能够直接用于另一个领域，从而无需为每个工具语料库单独训练一个模型。

sents.en: Transferability across tool domains.
sents.zh: 跨工具领域的可迁移性。

sents.en: A tool-selection model trained on one domain of tools should be usable directly on another, so that a separate model need not be trained for every tool corpus.
sents.zh: 在某一工具领域上训练的工具选择模型应当能够直接用于另一个领域，从而无需为每个工具语料库单独训练一个模型。

paragraphs.en: Transferability across retrievers. Some tools carry specific tool names and thus favor exact string matching, whereas other tools are better found by semantic matching, so the preferred retriever depends on the underlying tool corpus. We want the model to work under a new retriever without retraining.
paragraphs.zh: 跨检索器的可迁移性。 有些工具带有特定的工具名称，因而更适合精确字符串匹配，而另一些工具则更适合通过语义匹配来找到，因此首选的检索器取决于底层工具语料库。 我们希望模型在不重新训练的情况下能够在新的检索器下工作。

paragraphs.en: These challenges are tractable under the studied framework because tool selection is built on the generalizable skills of the underlying LLM: decomposing the user instruction and matching a tool description to it. The LLM needs no domain-specific knowledge, and the workflow stays invariant to different retrievers. We therefore fine-tune Qwen3 models ( Yang et al., 2025 ) with reinforcement learning to acquire these skills, and transfer them to new domains and retrievers (Figure 2 ).
paragraphs.zh: 在所研究的框架下，这些挑战是可解决的，因为工具选择建立在底层大语言模型的通用技能之上：分解用户指令并将工具描述与之匹配。 大语言模型不需要领域特定的知识，工作流对不同检索器保持不变。 因此，我们通过强化学习微调 Qwen3 模型（Yang et al., 2025）来习得这些技能，并将其迁移到新的领域和检索器（图 2）。

paragraphs.en: Standard RL assumes a fixed action set, whereas our actions are tools from a corpus that could change between training and deployment. Prior work handles large or changing action sets by learning action representations ( Dulac-Arnold et al., 2015 ; Chandak et al., 2019 ; Chandak et al., 2020 ) , and generalizes zero-shot to unseen actions by inferring their representations from action information acquired separately from the task ( Jain et al., 2020 ; Jain et al., 2022 ) . Our Select stage is such a policy over a varying action set of the retrieved tools, with each represented by its documentation. The LLM supplies these representations implicitly without a separately trained action encoder.
paragraphs.zh: 标准强化学习假设动作集合是固定的，而我们的动作是来自语料库的工具，该语料库在训练与部署之间可能发生变化。 已有工作通过学习动作表示来处理大型或变化的动作集（Dulac-Arnold et al., 2015；Chandak et al., 2019；Chandak et al., 2020），并通过从独立于任务获取的动作信息中推断其表示，实现对未见动作的零样本泛化（Jain et al., 2020；Jain et al., 2022）。 我们的 Select 阶段就是在这样一个由检索到的工具构成的变化动作集上的策略，其中每个动作都由其文档表示。 大语言模型隐式地提供这些表示，而无需单独训练的动作编码器。

paragraphs.en: Given a user instruction x x and a tool corpus 𝒯 \mathcal{T} too large to fit in the model’s context, tool selection asks for the subset T ⊆ 𝒯 T\subseteq\mathcal{T} of tools that x x requires. Rather than training a corpus-specific dense retriever, we let a single small model π \pi operate a lightweight, corpus-agnostic retriever ℛ \mathcal{R} to find these tools. We first define the workflow through which π \pi drives ℛ \mathcal{R} (§ 3.1 ), and then describe how π \pi is trained: supervised fine-tuning (§ 3.2 ) followed by reinforcement learning (§ 3.3 ). Unless otherwise stated, ℛ \mathcal{R} is BM25 ( Robertson and Zaragoza, 2009 ) , which requires no training and applies to any corpus. The transfer to new tool domains in § 4 therefore comes from the trained model rather than from a retriever fitted to the target corpus.

paragraphs.en: The LLM drives the retriever through a three-stage workflow (Figure 1 and Algorithm 1 ): a Plan stage decomposes the user instruction into substeps, a Retrieve stage fetches relevant candidates, and a Select stage chooses the tools it judges necessary, repeating until the instruction is covered.
paragraphs.zh: 大语言模型通过一个三阶段工作流驱动检索器（图 1 和算法 1）：规划阶段将用户指令分解为子步骤，检索阶段获取相关候选，选择阶段选出它判断必要的工具，并重复此过程直到指令被完全覆盖。

paragraphs.en: A user instruction often contains several requests. For instance, “book a flight from San Francisco to New York City and find a hotel in New York City” naturally splits into two. Because the retriever scores tools against the whole query, the terms of one request interfere with retrieval for the other. The model therefore first decomposes the instruction into an ordered list of substeps, each a short natural-language description of a single required capability.
paragraphs.zh: 用户指令通常包含多个请求。 例如，“预订一张从旧金山到纽约的航班并在纽约找一家酒店”自然地拆分为两个请求。 由于检索器是针对整个查询对工具进行评分，一个请求的词条会干扰另一个请求的检索。 因此，模型首先将该指令分解为一个有序的子步骤列表，每个子步骤是对单个所需能力的简短自然语言描述。

We use Llama-4-Maverick as the teacher model to create the training examples.

paragraphs.en: We assume access to a reference gold tool set for each query in the training data, but this set can be noisy. For instance, ToolBench ( Qin et al., 2024 ) collects gold tools from a reference solution trajectory, so some gold tools are not determined by anything the user wrote, and others are redundant near-duplicates. Training on such tools would teach the agent to select tools that the instruction does not call for. Therefore, our filter keeps a (query, gold tool) pair only if the tool can be identified from the query alone. A deterministic first pass keeps any pair whose query and tool documentation share a content word. The remaining pairs go to the teacher model, which keeps only those whose query contains a paraphrase or synonym of the tool’s function. The resulting curated gold set is used for both training and evaluation.
paragraphs.zh: 我们假设可以访问训练数据中每个查询的参考黄金工具集，但该集合可能含有噪声。 例如，ToolBench（Qin et al., 2024）从参考解法轨迹中收集黄金工具，因此一些黄金工具并非由用户所写的内容决定，而另一些则是冗余的近似重复项。 在这样的工具上训练会让智能体学会选择指令并未要求的工具。 因此，我们的过滤器仅在工具可以仅凭查询本身确定时，才保留该（查询，黄金工具）对。 确定性的第一遍筛选会保留查询与工具文档共享实词的任何对。 其余对交给教师模型，教师模型仅保留那些查询中包含工具功能的改写或同义表达的对。 由此得到的筛选后的黄金集同时用于训练和评估。

paragraphs.en: Given the surviving gold tools, the teacher model decomposes each user instruction into substeps, matching each substep to one of them. It may emit fewer substeps than gold tools, because some gold tools, though relevant, are unnecessary for the instruction. These unused gold tools are removed from the gold set as an additional round of filtering.

paragraphs.en: The generated substeps and the gold tools determine the tool-selection trajectory, but we still generate reasoning text so that the model can more easily learn how to act in the Plan and Select stages. For Plan , given the user instruction and the generated substeps, the teacher model writes the reasoning that justifies the decomposition. We do not reuse the teacher’s reasoning from the decomposition step itself, because the teacher saw the gold tools there and its reasoning would leak them. For Select , the teacher model writes the reasoning that justifies picking the gold tool among the candidates retrieved for the generated substep. A validation step flags any reasoning that names a tool outside the candidate set or leaks candidate indices, and triggers regeneration when a violation occurs.
paragraphs.zh: 生成的子步骤和标准工具共同决定了工具选择轨迹，但我们仍然生成推理文本，以便模型更容易学习如何在 Plan 和 Select 阶段行动。 对于 Plan，给定用户指令和生成的子步骤，教师模型撰写论证该分解合理性的推理。 我们不复用教师在分解步骤本身的推理，因为教师在那里看到了标准工具，其推理会泄露它们。 对于 Select，教师模型撰写论证在为生成子步骤检索到的候选中选择标准工具的推理。 验证步骤会标记任何提到候选集之外的工具或泄露候选索引的推理，并在出现违规时触发重新生成。

paragraphs.en: Starting from the SFT checkpoint, we further train the model with RL for better performance (§ 4 ). For training stability, we decouple Plan and Select into separate stages: when training Select , we use the high-quality substeps generated by the teacher model instead of the model’s own plans. Each stage is then a single stateless LLM call with its own reward, so we can train it with standard GRPO ( Shao et al., 2024 ) . The remaining question is how to design the Plan and Select rewards without additional human annotation.
paragraphs.zh: 从 SFT 检查点出发，我们进一步用强化学习（RL）训练模型以获得更好的性能（§ 4）。 为了训练稳定性，我们将 Plan 和 Select 解耦为两个独立阶段：训练 Select 时，我们使用教师模型生成的高质量子步骤，而不是模型自身的规划。 每个阶段都是一次无状态的 LLM 调用，并拥有自己的奖励，因此我们可以用标准的 GRPO（Shao et al., 2024）来训练它。 剩下的问题是如何在无需额外人工标注的情况下设计 Plan 和 Select 的奖励。

paragraphs.en: Our experiments answer three questions about the trained agent. (i) Success Rate. How does a small, locally-hosted tool-selection agent compare against inference-only baselines that drive the same task with a much larger, general-purpose model accessed by prompting alone (§ 4.1 )? (ii) Domain generalization. Does an agent trained on a single tool corpus transfer, with no retraining, to unseen corpora and domains (§ 4.2 )? (iii) Retriever generalization. Is the learned policy tied to the retriever it trained on, or can the retrieval backend be swapped at test time for a stronger, domain-specialized one (§ 4.3 )? To answer these questions, we train the Qwen3 model family at three model scales (1.7B, 4B, and 8B) on the ToolBench G3 ( Qin et al., 2024 ) training split, which contains 21,361 user instructions over a corpus of 1,419 APIs for the model to select. Each user instruction in this benchmark requires multiple tools and can be decomposed into several independent substeps, so it aligns with our assumption.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的实验回答了关于训练后智能体的三个问题。(i) 成功率。 一个小型的、本地部署的工具选择智能体，与仅通过推理的基线相比表现如何？后者仅依靠提示词驱动，使用体量大得多的通用模型完成相同任务（§ 4.1）？ (ii) 领域泛化。 在单一工具语料库上训练的智能体，能否在不重新训练的情况下迁移到未见过的语料库和领域（§ 4.2）？ (iii) 检索器泛化。 学到的策略是否与训练时使用的检索器绑定，还是可以在测试时将检索后端替换为更强的、领域专用的检索器（§ 4.3）？ 为了回答这些问题，我们在 ToolBench G3（Qin et al., 2024）训练集上以三种模型规模（1.7B、4B 和 8B）训练 Qwen3 模型系列，该训练集包含 21,361 条用户指令，模型需从中包含 1,419 个 API 的语料库中进行选择。 该基准中的每条用户指令都需要多个工具，并可分解为若干独立的子步骤，因此符合我们的假设。

sents.en: (iii) Retriever generalization.

sents.en: To answer these questions, we train the Qwen3 model family at three model scales (1.7B, 4B, and 8B) on the ToolBench G3 ( Qin et al., 2024 ) training split, which contains 21,361 user instructions over a corpus of 1,419 APIs for the model to select.

sents.en: Each user instruction in this benchmark requires multiple tools and can be decomposed into several independent substeps, so it aligns with our assumption.

paragraphs.en: We report evaluation results on the test split of ToolBench G3, which contains 2,124 user instructions. Success rate is defined with an exact-match metric: tool selection on one user instruction is considered successful if and only if the selected tool set matches exactly with the filtered gold tool set of § 3.2 , and the success rate is averaged over all tested user instructions. Prior work on tool retrieval mostly reports ranking metrics over the retrieved list, such as Recall@ K K and NDCG@ K K ( Qin et al., 2024 ; Qu et al., 2024 ; Shi et al., 2025 ) , or completeness, whether every gold tool appears in the top- K K ( Qu et al., 2024 ; Shi et al., 2025 ) . These credit a candidate list that contains the gold tools. Our metric is stricter: the agent must commit to a set, and both a missing tool and an extra tool count as a failure.
paragraphs.zh: 我们报告了在 ToolBench G3 测试集划分上的评估结果，该测试集包含 2,124 条用户指令。 成功率采用精确匹配指标定义：当且仅当针对某条用户指令所选的工具集合与 § 3.2 中过滤后的黄金工具集合完全一致时，该指令上的工具选择才被视为成功，成功率在所有被测用户指令上取平均。 以往关于工具检索的工作大多报告检索列表上的排序指标，例如 Recall@ K K 和 NDCG@ K K（Qin et al., 2024；Qu et al., 2024；Shi et al., 2025），或者完备性，即每个黄金工具是否都出现在 top- K K 中（Qu et al., 2024；Shi et al., 2025）。 这些指标会认可包含黄金工具的候选列表。 我们的指标更为严格：智能体必须确定地给出一个集合，无论是缺少工具还是多出工具都算作失败。

paragraphs.en: Figure 3 shows the effect of training: we compare the success rate of the untrained Qwen3 model, the model after SFT, and the model after SFT followed by RL (SFT+RL), at three scales. An untrained model performs poorly under our Plan – Retrieve – Select workflow. This is expected, as the model has not learned how to decompose user instructions and select tools. SFT alone raises the success rate above 30% at every scale, and RL improves it further (e.g., from 36.2% to 41.5% at 8B).
paragraphs.zh: 图 3 展示了训练的效果：我们在三个规模上比较了未经训练的 Qwen3 模型、经过 SFT 的模型以及经过 SFT 再加上 RL（SFT+RL）的模型的成功率。 未经训练的模型在我们的「规划 – 检索 – 选择」工作流下表现不佳。 这是符合预期的，因为模型尚未学会如何分解用户指令并选择工具。 仅使用 SFT 就能使每个规模下的成功率提升到 30% 以上，而 RL 进一步提升了成功率（例如在 8B 规模下从 36.2% 提升到 41.5%）。

paragraphs.en: ReAct , a ReAct style workflow following ToolReAGt ( Braunschweiler et al., 2025 ) . We use BM25 retriever and include plan decomposition to make a fair comparison with our workflow. After the same Plan stage as in our workflow, a ReAct loop is run for each substep: in every turn it writes its own search query, observes the BM25 top- K K candidates for that query, and either searches again (up to four times) or commits one tool. The union over substeps is the prediction. This differs from our workflow in two ways: 1) the model writes the retrieval query rather than reusing the substep text; 2) a substep may issue several retrievals rather than one.
paragraphs.zh: ReAct：一种遵循 ReAct 风格的工作流，参考 ToolReAGt（Braunschweiler et al., 2025）。 我们使用 BM25 检索器并加入计划分解，以便与我们的工作流进行公平比较。 在与我们工作流相同的计划阶段之后，对每个子步骤运行一个 ReAct 循环：在每一轮中，它自己撰写检索查询，观察该查询的 BM25 前 K 个候选结果，然后要么再次检索（最多四次），要么确定提交一个工具。 各子步骤结果的并集即为预测。 这与我们的工作流有两点不同：1）该模型自行撰写检索查询，而不是复用子步骤文本；2）一个子步骤可以发起多次检索，而不是一次。

paragraphs.en: Hierarchical search , following AnyTool ( Du et al., 2024 ) . No retriever is needed. Instead, the model walks the ToolBench taxonomy from category to tool to API, and a self-reflection turn re-enters the tree when the selection looks incomplete.

paragraphs.en: Table 1 shows that the Search-R1-style workflow pairs best with the untrained large model, reaching 30.6% success rate. paragraphs.en: A tool-selection agent is only useful if it works on corpora it was not trained on, so we test the models trained on ToolBench G3 directly on four benchmarks. We choose them to probe two independent axes of transferability: how far the tool corpus and domain shift from the training distribution, and whether the task needs a single tool or several . ToolBench G2 is the mildest shift: a larger, mostly-disjoint split of the same RapidAPI universe (11,474 tools, only ∼ \sim 9% shared with G3) in the same multi-tool scenario. Gorilla ( Patil et al., 2024 ) and CRAFT ( Yuan et al., 2024 ) come from entirely different tool repositories and domains, exercising a much larger vocabulary shift. All user instructions in both benchmarks have exactly one gold tool, so no Plan stage is needed and thus we focus on the transferability of the Select stage. Finally TaskBench ( Shen et al., 2024 ) is the multi-tool out-of-domain case: tasks from entirely different domains that each require several tools, evaluated over each split’s own tool inventory, so it is a comprehensive evaluation of both planning and selection.
paragraphs.zh: 工具选择智能体只有在未训练过的语料库上也能工作才有用，因此我们将基于 ToolBench G3 训练的模型直接在四个基准上进行测试。 我们选择这些基准是为了考察两个独立的可迁移性维度：工具语料库和领域偏离训练分布的程度，以及任务需要单个工具还是多个工具。 ToolBench G2 是最轻微的偏移：它是同一 RapidAPI 宇宙中一个更大且基本不相交的划分（11,474 个工具，与 G3 仅约 ∼ \sim 9% 共享），且处于相同的多工具场景中。 Gorilla（Patil et al., 2024）和 CRAFT（Yuan et al., 2024）来自完全不同的工具仓库和领域，带来大得多的词汇表偏移。 两个基准中的所有用户指令都恰好对应一个金标工具，因此无需 Plan 阶段，从而我们将重点放在 Select 阶段的可迁移性上。 最后，TaskBench（Shen et al., 2024）是多工具域外案例：来自完全不同领域且各自需要多个工具的任务，并在每个划分自身的工具清单上进行评估，因此它是对规划与选择能力的综合评估。

paragraphs.en: The results are shown in Table 2 . On ToolBench G2 the trained agent transfers, though below its in-domain G3 score ( ∼ \sim 24% vs. 40% at 4B). The 8 × 8\times larger, mostly-disjoint corpus adds distractors and pushes gold deeper into the BM25 ranking. Even so, it beats the strongest untrained baseline (Maverick + Search-R1, 20.8%). The same checkpoints have a clear transfer advantage on single-tool benchmarks (Gorilla and CRAFT) over Llama-4-Maverick, so the Select stage transfers across domains. The only exception happens on TaskBench, in which Llama-4-Maverick with the Search-R1-style workflow gives an 8 pp higher success rate than our method. This shows that the Plan stage requires some domain knowledge and thus the Search-R1-style workflow, which requires no decomposition, performs better. Nonetheless, our small model still beats Llama-4-Maverick on ReAct and our workflow, which both include a Plan stage.

paragraphs.en: Tool selection over a large tool corpus is a recurring sub-routine of agentic tool calling, and prior work runs it by prompting proprietary models to operate a retriever. We showed that this capability can be trained into a small open model. Under a minimal Plan – Retrieve – Select workflow, supervised warm-up on teacher-written trajectories followed by RL with a retrieval-based planning reward and an exact-match selection reward lifts Qwen3 models of 1.7B to 8B parameters past Llama-4-Maverick (402B) on ToolBench G3, with no human annotation beyond the gold tool sets. Because the skills involved, i.e., instruction decomposition and tool selection from description, are not tied to a specific tool corpus, the same checkpoints transfer without retraining to new tool domains and to new retrievers, inheriting the stronger retriever’s recall. We hope this work encourages further study of tool selection with small LLMs.
paragraphs.zh: 在大规模工具语料上进行工具选择是智能体工具调用中反复出现的子例程，先前的工作通过提示专有模型来操作检索器来完成这一任务。 我们证明了这种能力可以被训练到小规模开源模型中。 在一个极简的规划–检索–选择工作流下，先对教师撰写的轨迹进行监督式热身，再使用基于检索的规划奖励和精确匹配选择奖励进行强化学习，使参数量从 1.7B 到 8B 的 Qwen3 模型在 ToolBench G3 上超越了 Llama-4-Maverick（402B），且除黄金工具集外无需任何人工标注。 由于所涉及的技能，即指令分解和根据描述进行工具选择，并不依赖于特定的工具语料，相同的检查点无需重新训练即可迁移到新的工具领域和新的检索器上，并继承更强检索器的召回能力。 我们希望这项工作能鼓励对小规模大语言模型工具选择的进一步研究。

paragraphs.en: We train Qwen3-1.7B, Qwen3-4B, and Qwen3-8B. Qwen3 can emit a <think> block before its answer, and our trained models use this block for the brief reasoning that precedes each JSON action: the SFT targets place the teacher-written rationale inside <think> … </think> followed by the action (Appendix D ), and the SFT and SFT+RL models are run with thinking enabled during SFT, RL, and evaluation. The reasoning they produce is therefore the short, task-specific rationale learned in SFT and shaped by RL, not Qwen3’s open-ended native deliberation. The untrained Qwen3 models (the Base rows of § 4.1 , the untrained planner of § 4.4 , and the RL-only ablation, which starts from the base model) are instead run with thinking disabled ( enable_thinking=False ), because the base model’s native thinking block routinely exhausted the generation budget before producing an action. A single model serves both the Plan and Select stages.

paragraphs.en: Llama-4-Maverick is a mixture-of-experts model with 128 experts, 17B active parameters, and 402B total parameters, so it is roughly two orders of magnitude larger than our largest trained model in total parameters and twice as large in active parameters. It plays two roles. It is the teacher for gold filtering, plan decomposition, and reasoning generation in the data curation pipeline of § 3.2 , and it is the prompted model behind all four inference-only baselines of § 4.1 .

paragraphs.en: The default retriever is BM25 implemented with the bm25s library ( Lù, 2024 ) (Lucene scoring variant) using k 1 = 1.8 k_{1}=1.8 and b = 1.0 b=1.0 , English stopword removal, and no stemming. Each tool is indexed by its serialized documentation entry (tool and API name, description, and parameter fields). paragraphs.en: Table 3 summarizes the corpora. ToolBench G3 ( Qin et al., 2024 ) is the training benchmark: its corpus has 1,419 RapidAPI tools, the training split has 21,361 user instructions, and the test split has 2,124. Every instruction requires multiple tools and decomposes into several independent substeps. All training, the main results, the ablations, and the retriever-swap experiment use G3. ToolBench G2 is a larger, mostly disjoint split of the same RapidAPI universe (11,474 tools, about 9% shared with G3) in the same multi-tool setting; we evaluate the 7,238 test instructions that survive the same gold filtering as G3 (§ 3.2 ). Gorilla ( Patil et al., 2024 ) covers tool calls to three machine-learning model hubs, with one source split each ( huggingface , pytorch , tensor ; 500, 43, and 55 instructions). CRAFT ( Yuan et al., 2024 ) covers tool use for math, tabular, and visual question answering ( math-algebra , tabmwp , vqa ; 280, 174, and 200 instructions). Every Gorilla and CRAFT instruction has exactly one gold tool. TaskBench ( Shen et al., 2024 ) is the multi-tool out-of-domain case: three source splits ( daily , multimedia , huggingface ; 103 instructions in total), each with its own small inventory of 23–40 tools, where each instruction requires several tools (2.6 on average). ToolBench G2 and G3 use the retrieval splits released with ToolBench. Gorilla, CRAFT, and TaskBench use the packaging of ToolRet ( Shi et al., 2025 ) , which provides instruction-framed queries and a unified corpus format; we restrict each split’s corpus to its own source’s tool inventory rather than ToolRet’s merged corpus, matching the original benchmarks. All user instructions and tool documentation in every benchmark are in English. The G3 test split has 2,373 instructions, of which 2,124 (89.5%) survive the gold filtering of § 3.2 ; the G2 test split has 8,250, of which 7,238 (87.7%) survive. Gorilla, CRAFT, and TaskBench are evaluated on their original gold labels without filtering.

paragraphs.en: All training uses the ToolBench G3 ( Qin et al., 2024 ) training split only. The split has 21,361 instructions with 57,836 (instruction, gold tool) pairs, i.e., 2.71 gold tools per instruction. The gold tool filtering of § 3.2 keeps 54,695 pairs (94.6%); the plan decomposition step then drops a further 1,928 gold tools that the teacher judges unnecessary for the instruction. In total 1,268 instructions (5.9%) are discarded, either because no gold tool survives or because the teacher fails the output validation three times, leaving 20,093 curated training instructions. The SFT corpus built from them contains 19,841 Plan examples and 38,293 Select examples, each a single (prompt, reasoning + action) pair. A held-out slice of 119 training instructions (with its 783 SFT examples) serves as a validation set during development. The RL prompt set is derived from the same curated instructions: one Plan prompt per instruction and one Select prompt per teacher-written substep.

paragraphs.en: All results report the exact-match success rate of § 4.1 : an instruction counts as a success if and only if the union of selected tool IDs over all substeps equals the filtered gold tool set. All numbers are from a single run; repeated runs of the same checkpoint differ by one to two instructions because of non-deterministic batched inference.

paragraphs.en: All four protocols of § 4.1 prompt the same Llama-4-Maverick (Appendix A.1 ) with greedy decoding and at most 1,024 new tokens per call (2,048 for our workflow).
paragraphs.zh: § 4.1 的全部四种协议均以贪心解码方式提示同一个 Llama-4-Maverick（附录 A.1），每次调用最多生成 1,024 个新 token（我们的工作流为 2,048 个）。

paragraphs.en: ReAct first decomposes the instruction into at most five substeps with a prompt that includes two few-shot decomposition examples, then runs one ReAct loop per substep over BM25: Each turn the model sees the substep, its search history, and the top-10 results of its latest search, and chooses to search again, select one tool, or skip; the loop may issue at most four searches before committing.
paragraphs.zh: ReAct 首先通过一个包含两个少样本分解示例的提示词，将指令分解为最多五个子步骤，然后在 BM25 上为每个子步骤运行一次 ReAct 循环：每一轮，智能体会看到该子步骤、其搜索历史以及其最新搜索的前 10 条结果，并选择再次搜索、选择一个工具，或跳过；该循环在提交答案之前最多可执行四次搜索。

paragraphs.en: Hierarchical search follows AnyTool ( Du et al., 2024 ) : the model descends the ToolBench category → \to tool → \to API taxonomy (G3: 36 categories and 241 tools; G2: 49 categories and 3,391 tools), choosing at most 3 categories, 6 tools per category, and 15 APIs per tool, with API descriptions truncated to 200 characters, and re-enters the tree after one self-reflection round.
paragraphs.zh: 分层搜索遵循 AnyTool（Du et al., 2024）：模型沿 ToolBench 的类别 → \to 工具 → \to API 分类树逐层下探（G3：36 个类别和 241 个工具；G2：49 个类别和 3,391 个工具），最多选择 3 个类别、每个类别 6 个工具、每个工具 15 个 API，API 描述截断为 200 个字符，并在一轮自我反思后重新进入该树。

paragraphs.en: Search-R1-style follows Jin et al. (2025) : a single generation interleaving <think> , <search> (BM25 top-10 per search, at most six searches), and a final <answer> containing the tool set, with no decomposition; the prompt includes one three-turn worked example, and generation is stopped at each </search> tag so the model cannot fabricate retrieval results.
paragraphs.zh: Search-R1 风格遵循 Jin 等人 (2025)：单次生成中交替使用 <think>、<search>（每次搜索返回 BM25 前 10 条，最多搜索六次）以及包含工具集合的最终 <answer>，不进行任务分解；提示词中包含一个三轮的示例演示，并且生成在每个 </search> 标签处停止，以防止模型编造检索结果。

paragraphs.en: This work creates three derived artifacts: the curated gold tool sets and teacher-written SFT trajectories for ToolBench G3 and G2 (§ 3.2 ), the trained Qwen3 checkpoints, and the training and evaluation code. Because the SFT data are generated with Llama-4-Maverick, the trained checkpoints are derivatives of Llama outputs. None of these artifacts are released, and they are used only for the experiments reported here. The intended use of the trained models is research on tool selection; they are not validated for deployment in agents that execute consequential actions. All information needed to re-implement the pipeline, including prompts (Appendix D ), hyperparameters (Table 4 ), software versions (Appendix A.2 ), and data statistics, is reported in this paper.
paragraphs.zh: 本工作创建了三个派生产物：为 ToolBench G3 和 G2 精心整理的黄金工具集以及教师撰写的 SFT 轨迹（§ 3.2）、训练得到的 Qwen3 检查点，以及训练与评估代码。 由于 SFT 数据由 Llama-4-Maverick 生成，训练得到的检查点是 Llama 输出的衍生品。 这些产物均未公开发布，仅用于本文所报告的实验。 训练得到模型的预期用途是工具选择研究；它们尚未经过验证，不可用于执行重大后果动作的智能体部署。 重新实现该流程所需的全部信息，包括提示词（附录 D）、超参数（表 4）、软件版本（附录 A.2）以及数据统计，均已在本文中报告。
